features.name: Embedded PostgreSQL test harness
features.summary: Provides disposable, self-contained PostgreSQL clusters for the test suite: it allocates a free port (skipping reserved Paperclip ports), initializes a temp data directory, and starts an embedded-postgres instance with bounded retry. Failures surface the real Postgres output captured in a bounded log buffer, shutdown is time-bounded so test hooks never hang, and data directories are reclaimed only after the process actually exits. A support probe reports whether the embedded runtime works on the current machine before tests depend on it.

features.name: Allowlisted Google Sheets agent tools
features.summary: Exposes Google Sheets operations (list, read, search, append, update, add tab, clear, delete rows) as MCP tools that agents can call, with every operation gated by a configured spreadsheet-ID allowlist. Each tool carries MCP risk annotations (read-only vs destructive hints) so clients can gate dangerous calls, validates input through strict zod schemas (single-line A1 ranges, bounded row counts), and redacts configured secrets from error responses before they reach the model.

features.name: Agent-facing MCP toolset for issues, approvals, and workspaces
features.summary: Wraps the platform's core API as typed MCP tools an agent can invoke: identity and inbox lookup, issue list/create/update/checkout, comments, versioned markdown documents, and approval creation with approve/reject/requestRevision/resubmit decisions. It also powers issue-thread interactions — suggesting tasks, asking the user questions, and requesting (checkbox) confirmations — each with idempotency keys and continuation policies that can wake the assignee agent. Finally it exposes execution-workspace runtime control: start/stop/restart services by ID or name and poll until a service is actually ready, with a bounded wait timeout.

features.name: Plugin project scaffolding
features.summary: Generates a complete starter project for new Paperclip plugins from a template (default, connector, workspace, environment), including manifest/worker/UI entry points, package.json, tsconfig, esbuild and rollup configs built from the SDK's bundler presets, and vitest setup. It validates npm-style plugin names and categories, refuses to overwrite an existing directory, and wires the plugin SDK either as a workspace dependency inside the monorepo or as a locally packed tarball outside it. Generated scripts include a watch-mode build and a dev server for hot-reloading the plugin UI.

features.name: Plugin UI animation showcase
features.summary: An example plugin UI component (kitchen-sink demo) that renders a living ASCII-art scene of paperclip sprites drifting across a monospace character grid with motion trails and ambient waves. It throttles rendering to 24 FPS via requestAnimationFrame with delta-scaled physics on typed-array grids, rebuilds the grid from measured glyph metrics when the container resizes, and gracefully degrades to a static frame when prefers-reduced-motion is set or the tab is hidden. It demonstrates the capabilities and performance discipline available to third-party plugin UIs.

files.summary: Test-support module that launches disposable embedded PostgreSQL clusters for the test suite. It handles free-port allocation (avoiding reserved Paperclip ports), temp data-directory lifecycle, bounded-retry startup with real Postgres log capture, and a time-bounded graceful stop so test hooks never hang.
behavior: Allocates a random free TCP port via a bind-probe loop that retries up to 20 times, rejecting any port in the reserved set (default 54329 plus PAPERCLIP_EMBEDDED_POSTGRES_PORT and PAPERCLIP_TEST_POSTGRES_RESERVED_PORTS).

Retries cluster startup up to 5 attempts, each with a fresh port and fresh temp data dir; on final failure it throws an error that includes recent Postgres output captured from a bounded log buffer, because start() rejections carry empty messages.

Bounds the graceful stop wait at 5000ms via Promise.race so vitest afterAll hooks complete, and chains data-dir removal on the raw stop() promise so files are only deleted after the Postgres child process has actually exited.

Exposes a support probe (getEmbeddedPostgresTestSupport) that starts and immediately tears down a cluster to report {supported, reason}, plus test-only seams to replace the embedded-postgres constructor provider.

files.summary: Defines the MCP tool surface for a Google Sheets server: list spreadsheets, get metadata, read/search values, append/update rows, add sheet tabs, and clear values or delete rows. Every tool is schema-validated, allowlist-gated, risk-annotated, and its errors are secret-redacted before returning to the caller.
behavior: Rejects any operation whose spreadsheetId is not in the configured allowlist (trimmed, deduped, non-empty), throwing 'Spreadsheet ... is not in the configured allowlist.'

Attaches MCP ToolAnnotations per risk tier: read tools get readOnlyHint=true; write tools get destructiveHint=false; clear_values and delete_rows are marked destructive, and delete_rows additionally validates endIndex > startIndex.
Redacts configured secrets (values of length >= 8) from error text by string replacement with [REDACTED] before returning isError tool results.
Validates inputs with zod: ranges must be single-line A1 notation <= 500 chars, search is case-insensitive by default with maxResults capped at 500, and valueInputOption defaults to RAW.

files.summary: Core MCP server tool definitions that expose the Paperclip platform API to agents: actor/inbox identity, issue list/create/update/checkout, comments, versioned markdown documents, approval creation and decisions, issue-thread interactions (suggest tasks, ask questions, request confirmations), a raw API-request passthrough, and execution-workspace runtime control. Each tool zod-validates input and returns formatted text or error content via PaperclipApiClient.
behavior: Wraps REST endpoints as named tools (paperclipMe, paperclipInboxLite, paperclipListIssues with ~16 filter params, createIssue, updateIssue, checkoutIssue, addComment, upsertDocument with baseRevisionId for optimistic versioning, approval create/decide with approve|reject|requestRevision|resubmit actions).

Creates issue-thread interactions — suggestTasks, askUserQuestions, requestConfirmation, requestCheckboxConfirmation — each accepting idempotencyKey, sourceCommentId/sourceRunId provenance, and a continuationPolicy (default 'wake_assignee' or 'none') that controls whether the assignee agent is re-engaged.

Controls issue workspace runtimes: start/stop/restart by workspaceCommandId, runtimeServiceId, or serviceIndex; fetches heartbeat-context to read currentExecutionWorkspace.runtimeServices and selects a service by ID, name, or first running/starting instance.
Waits for a workspace service to be ready by polling with sleep() up to a caller-supplied timeoutSeconds (max 300).

files.summary: Scaffolding engine for new Paperclip plugin projects. It validates plugin names and categories, resolves a template (default/connector/workspace/environment), and writes a complete starter repo: package.json with paperclipPlugin manifest/worker/ui entries, tsconfig, esbuild and rollup configs from SDK bundler presets, vitest config, and dev scripts including a hot-reload UI dev server.
behavior: Validates npm-style plugin names (scoped or lowercase unscoped) against regex patterns, rejects invalid template/category values with explicit messages, and refuses to scaffold if the output directory already exists.

Derives idiomatic metadata from the package name: strips the scope for the directory name, converts '@scope/name' to 'scope.name' for the manifest id, and title-cases tokens for the default display name.

When scaffolding outside the monorepo, builds and packs the local SDK and @paperclipai/shared packages with pnpm into a .paperclip-sdk tarball directory and references them via file: dependencies (with pnpm overrides); inside the repo it uses workspace:*.

Generates esbuild.config.mjs and rollup.config.mjs using createPluginBundlerPresets for worker, manifest, and UI bundles, with a --watch mode and a 'dev:ui' script invoking paperclip-plugin-dev-server on port 4177.

files.summary: A React component for the kitchen-sink example plugin that renders an animated ASCII-art scene: paperclip sprites drift across a monospace character grid over an ambient sine-wave background, leaving fading motion trails. It is performance- and accessibility-disciplined: fixed 24 FPS via requestAnimationFrame, typed-array grids, resize-driven rebuilds, and a static-frame fallback for reduced-motion or hidden tabs.
behavior: Throttles rendering to 24 FPS (FRAME_INTERVAL_MS gate inside a requestAnimationFrame loop) with delta-scaled sprite physics (wobble via sin/cos drift, damping at 0.998, alpha fade-in/out over the first/last 12% of each sprite's life).

Maintains the scene in Float32Array/Uint16Array buffers (trail decay 0.92 per frame, clipMask char codes) and skips DOM writes entirely when the composed output string is unchanged from the last frame.
Measures the monospace glyph cell with a hidden span and uses a ResizeObserver to rebuild the grid (cols/rows/buffers) when the container resizes, dropping out-of-bounds clips.

Stops the animation loop and renders a single static frame (ambient pattern plus tiled paperclip sprites) when prefers-reduced-motion matches or document.visibilityState is hidden, and cleans up all observers/listeners on unmount.
